description: Structured Action Plan system â€” API capabilities exposed through the runner's UI Bridge endpoints. The action plan endpoint (POST /ui-bridge/control/action-plan) accepts ordered arrays of typed UI actions with multi-strategy element resolution, confidence-based filtering, and per-action error handling. Successful plans are cached by page URL and element fingerprint via GET/POST /ui-bridge/control/action-plan/cache. The AI snapshot endpoint (GET /ui-bridge/ai/snapshot) supports token budget pruning via the maxTokens query parameter, prioritizing main-content elements over peripheral regions. All features operate on the runner's own UI and are verifiable by calling UI Bridge endpoints and inspecting responses. Data arrives via Tauri IPC events (ui-bridge-request / ui-bridge-response) between the Rust backend and the React frontend. The action plan handler (mcp/ui_bridge.rs) dispatches to ui_bridge_request_sync for each action. The cache (mcp/action_plan_cache.rs) is an in-memory LRU store. Token budget pruning runs in the frontend's SemanticSnapshotManager (ui-bridge/src/ai/semantic-snapshot.ts).

groups.name: Action Plan API Reachability
groups.description: The action plan system is a set of HTTP endpoints on the runner's API server (port 9876). When the runner is running, these endpoints are reachable. The runner UI must be fully loaded with registered elements for the action plan to have targets to act on. The runner's sidebar navigation, tab buttons, and interactive controls serve as the element pool that action plans operate against.

assertions.description: The runner UI is fully loaded with interactive elements registered in the UI Bridge element registry, confirming that the API server is running and action plans have targets to operate on

The runner sidebar contains multiple navigation tabs (Workflows, Active, Terminal, etc.) that serve as reliable element targets for action plan testing â€” each is a registered button with a stable elementId

groups.name: Runner UI Element Inventory
groups.description: The action plan system requires a populated element registry to function. The runner UI must contain a sufficient inventory of interactive elements (buttons, inputs, tabs) and content elements (headings, status text, badges) for action plans to target. A snapshot of the runner UI should return at least 20 registered elements, providing a diverse pool of targets for elementId, searchText, and testId resolution strategies.

assertions.description: The runner UI snapshot contains at least 20 registered elements, providing sufficient targets for action plan testing across multiple resolution strategies
assertions.notes: The runner UI typically has 30-70 buttons depending on the active view. Count assertion checks at least 10 buttons exist.

assertions.description: The runner UI displays a heading identifying the application, confirming the page has fully rendered with content elements available for text-based action plan targeting
The runner UI contains a terminal input textarea, which is a complex interactive element that action plans can target for type, sendKeys, and focus actions

groups.name: Action Plan Click Interactions
groups.description: The action plan endpoint executes click actions on registered elements by resolving the target (via elementId, searchText, testId, or CSS selector), then dispatching a click via IPC to the frontend's action executor. The click action produces a result with success=true, the resolvedElementId, post-action elementState (including computed styles, visibility, rect, and text content), and durationMs. Clicking a sidebar tab should cause the runner to navigate to that section, which can be verified by taking a snapshot after the action plan completes and checking for section-specific elements. The action plan endpoint is POST /ui-bridge/control/action-plan, powered by ui_bridge_execute_action_plan_handler in mcp/ui_bridge.rs.

assertions.description: Users can execute a click action by specifying a direct elementId from a prior snapshot. The action plan response shows success=true with the resolvedElementId matching the target and durationMs indicating execution time
assertions.expected: POST /ui-bridge/control/action-plan with {actions:[{action:'click', target:{elementId:'button-active-1'}, confidence:0.95}]} returns {success:true, results:[{success:true, resolvedElementId:'button-active-1'}]}

assertions.description: Users can execute a click action by specifying searchText and elementType. The find handler performs fuzzy text matching against element labels and text content, resolving to the best-matching element. The response includes the resolvedElementId that was found via search

target.label: Terminal tab button (findable via searchText='Terminal' + elementType='button')

assertions.expected: POST /ui-bridge/control/action-plan with {actions:[{action:'click', target:{searchText:'Terminal', elementType:'button'}, confidence:0.9}]} returns {success:true, results:[{resolvedElementId: starts with 'button-terminal'}]}

assertions.description: When an action targets a nonexistent elementId, the action fails with an error message containing 'not found' and the response shows success=false for that action. With stopOnFailure=true (default), subsequent actions are not executed

target.label: Any button (failure test uses a fabricated elementId)

assertions.expected: POST /ui-bridge/control/action-plan with {actions:[{action:'click', target:{elementId:'nonexistent-xyz'}}]} returns {success:false, failedCount:1, results:[{success:false, error: contains 'not found'}]}

groups.name: Multi-Step Action Plan Execution
groups.description: Action plans can contain multiple actions executed sequentially. Each action's result is independent â€” one action's failure does not retroactively change a prior action's success. The plan supports mixing different action types (click, wait, navigate) and different resolution strategies (elementId for one, searchText for another) in a single request. The response's executedCount + skippedCount + failedCount always equals the total number of actions in the plan (or fewer if stopOnFailure halted early). The wait action pauses execution for params.ms milliseconds (capped at 30,000ms) without requiring an element target.

assertions.description: Users can execute multiple actions in a single plan request. Actions execute in array order and the response contains one result per action with independent success/failure status

target.label: OBSERVE button (second target in a multi-step plan)

assertions.expected: A plan with 3 actions returns results array of length 3 with executedCount=3 when all succeed

assertions.description: Users can insert wait actions between click actions to allow UI transitions to complete. The wait action's durationMs in the response matches the requested ms value, and subsequent actions execute after the delay

target.label: Any button (wait action doesn't target elements)

assertions.expected: A plan with [{action:'wait', params:{ms:500}}, {action:'click', target:{elementId:'...'}}] returns totalDurationMs >= 500 with both results showing success=true

assertions.description: When stopOnFailure is true and an action fails, the plan halts and returns partial results. The results array length equals the index of the failed action + 1, not the total plan length

target.label: Any button (stopOnFailure tested with a nonexistent target)

assertions.expected: A plan with [failingAction, successAction] and stopOnFailure=true returns results with length 1 and failedCount=1

assertions.description: When stopOnFailure is false, all actions execute regardless of individual failures. The response shows the full results array with mixed success/failure statuses
assertions.expected: A plan with [failingAction, successAction] and stopOnFailure=false returns results with length 2, failedCount=1, executedCount=1

groups.name: Confidence-Based Action Filtering
groups.description: Each planned action carries a confidence score (0.0â€“1.0, default 1.0). The plan-level confidenceThreshold (default 0.5) determines which actions execute: actions with confidence >= threshold execute normally, actions below threshold are skipped. Skipped actions appear in results with skippedLowConfidence=true and durationMs=0. The threshold is evaluated before element resolution, so skipped actions never attempt to find their target. This is an automatic behavior â€” no user interaction required.

assertions.description: The action plan automatically skips actions with confidence below the threshold. The skipped action's result shows skippedLowConfidence=true, no resolvedElementId, and durationMs=0

target.label: Any button (confidence filtering is API behavior)

assertions.expected: A plan with [{confidence:0.9}, {confidence:0.1}] and confidenceThreshold=0.5 returns executedCount=1, skippedCount=1. Second result has skippedLowConfidence=true

assertions.description: Actions without an explicit confidence field default to 1.0, ensuring they always execute regardless of the threshold setting
assertions.expected: A plan with [{action:'click', target:{elementId:'...'}}] (no confidence field) executes successfully with skippedLowConfidence=false

groups.name: Action Plan Input Validation
groups.description: The action plan endpoint validates input before execution. Plans with more than 50 actions are rejected with HTTP 400. Empty plans (0 actions) return immediate success with executedCount=0. These are automatic behaviors enforced by the endpoint handler.

assertions.description: An empty action plan (actions=[]) returns immediate success with executedCount=0, skippedCount=0, failedCount=0, and totalDurationMs near 0
assertions.expected: POST /ui-bridge/control/action-plan with {actions:[]} returns {success:true, executedCount:0, totalDurationMs:0}

assertions.description: Plans with more than 50 actions are rejected with HTTP 400 status code before any action is attempted
assertions.expected: POST /ui-bridge/control/action-plan with 51 actions returns HTTP 400

groups.name: Action Plan Response Data Format
groups.description: The action plan response contains structured data about the execution. Each per-action result includes: index (position in array), success (boolean), action (type string), resolvedElementId (the element that was found and acted on), error (message if failed), skippedLowConfidence (boolean), durationMs (execution time), and elementState (post-action DOM state including computedStyles, rect, textContent, visible, enabled). The aggregate response includes: success (all-pass boolean), goal (echoed from request), results (array), executedCount, skippedCount, failedCount, totalDurationMs, and cached (whether stored in cache). This data format is defined in Rust as ActionPlanResponse/PlannedActionResult (mcp/ui_bridge.rs) and in TypeScript as ActionPlanResult/PlannedActionResult (qontinui-schemas/ts/src/workflow/action-plan.ts).

assertions.description: Each action result in the response contains index, success, action, durationMs, and skippedLowConfidence fields. Successful actions additionally contain resolvedElementId and elementState

target.label: RUN button (target for verifying result data format)

assertions.expected: Response result object contains: {index: 0, success: true, action: 'click', resolvedElementId: 'button-run', durationMs: number, skippedLowConfidence: false, elementState: {visible: true, enabled: true, textContent: string, rect: {x,y,width,height}}}

assertions.description: The aggregate response shows executedCount + skippedCount + failedCount equaling the total number of results, with totalDurationMs reflecting wall-clock time for the entire plan
assertions.expected: Response contains {executedCount: N, skippedCount: M, failedCount: K} where N+M+K equals results.length, and totalDurationMs >= sum of individual durationMs values

assertions.description: Failed actions include descriptive error messages that identify what went wrong. Element resolution failures say 'Element resolution failed: No element target specified or element not found'. IPC failures include the transport error
assertions.expected: A failed action's result contains error field with a human-readable message, e.g., 'Element resolution failed: ...' or 'Element not found: ...'

groups.name: Action Plan Cache State
groups.description: The action plan cache is an in-memory LRU store (max 100 entries, 1-hour TTL) that persists successful action plans for cross-run reuse. Cache state is queryable via two endpoints: GET /ui-bridge/control/action-plan/cache (lookup by URL + element fingerprint) and GET /ui-bridge/control/action-plan/cache/stats (entry count, total hits). Cache keys are derived from normalized page URL (scheme+host+path, no query/fragment) and an order-independent element fingerprint (FNV-1a hash of id+type+role+label per element, sorted). The cache is populated automatically when action plans include pageUrl and elementSnapshot fields and execution succeeds. Failed plans are evicted. The cache is backed by a global LazyLock<ActionPlanCache> singleton in mcp/action_plan_cache.rs.

assertions.description: The cache stores a plan when the request includes pageUrl and elementSnapshot and all actions succeed. The response shows cached=true and subsequent GET /cache/stats shows totalEntries incremented by 1

target.label: RUN button (target for a cacheable plan)

assertions.expected: After POST action-plan with pageUrl+elementSnapshot+successful click, GET /cache/stats shows totalEntries >= 1 and the response had cached=true

assertions.description: The cache returns a hit when queried with the same URL and element snapshot that was used to store a plan. The response includes hit=true, the full plan array, goal string, hitCount (incremented each lookup), and lastSuccess=true
assertions.expected: GET /cache?url=<same>&elements=<same> returns {hit:true, plan:[...], goal:'...', hitCount: >=1, lastSuccess:true}
assertions.precondition: At least one action plan with pageUrl and elementSnapshot has been successfully executed since the runner started

assertions.description: The cache returns a miss when queried with a URL or element snapshot that has never been cached. The response contains only hit=false
assertions.expected: GET /cache?url=http://never-cached&elements=[{"id":"x"}] returns {hit:false}

assertions.description: The cache does not store plans that failed. If a previously cached plan fails on re-execution, it is evicted from the cache
assertions.expected: After POST action-plan with pageUrl+elementSnapshot targeting nonexistent element (fails), GET /cache with same params returns {hit:false}

assertions.description: The cache stats endpoint shows the current state of the cache: totalEntries (number of stored plans), totalHits (cumulative lookup hits), maxEntries (100), and ttlSeconds (3600)
assertions.expected: GET /cache/stats returns {totalEntries: number, totalHits: number, maxEntries: 100, ttlSeconds: 3600}

groups.name: Token Budget Snapshot Pruning
groups.description: The AI snapshot endpoint (GET /ui-bridge/ai/snapshot) accepts a maxTokens query parameter. When maxTokens is a positive number, the SemanticSnapshotManager in the frontend sorts elements by region priority (main-content:100, form:90, modal:85, table:80, card:75, toolbar:70, navigation:50, sidebar:40, header:30, footer:20, unknown:10) with boosts for interactive (+20), visible (+10), and focused (+30) elements, then greedily includes elements until the token budget is exceeded. Token estimation uses ~4 characters per token. When maxTokens=0 or absent, all elements are included. The maxTokens parameter flows: HTTP query param -> Rust AiSnapshotQuery -> IPC payload.maxTokens -> React useAISearchEvents handler -> SemanticSnapshotManager({maxTokens}) -> applyTokenBudget(). Source files: mcp/ui_bridge.rs (AiSnapshotQuery, ui_bridge_ai_snapshot_handler), ui-bridge/src/ai/semantic-snapshot.ts (applyTokenBudget, REGION_PRIORITY), runner/src/hooks/ui-bridge-events/useAISearchEvents.ts (ai_snapshot case).

assertions.description: The AI snapshot returns all registered elements when maxTokens is not provided, matching the element count from a control snapshot

target.label: Any button (element count verified via API)

assertions.expected: GET /ai/snapshot returns elements array with length matching GET /control/snapshot elements count (typically 40-70 elements)

assertions.description: maxTokens=0 produces the same result as no maxTokens parameter, confirming that 0 means unlimited rather than empty
assertions.expected: GET /ai/snapshot and GET /ai/snapshot?maxTokens=0 return the same elements count

assertions.description: The AI snapshot returns fewer elements when maxTokens is smaller than the full snapshot's estimated token count, with main-content and interactive elements preserved while footer and unknown-region elements are dropped first
assertions.expected: GET /ai/snapshot?maxTokens=500 returns fewer elements than GET /ai/snapshot (typically 3-7 elements vs 40-70). GET /ai/snapshot?maxTokens=2000 returns an intermediate count

assertions.description: Element counts increase monotonically as maxTokens increases: maxTokens=200 <= maxTokens=500 <= maxTokens=1000 <= maxTokens=2000 <= maxTokens=5000 <= unlimited
assertions.expected: A series of GET /ai/snapshot?maxTokens=N requests with increasing N produces non-decreasing element counts

groups.name: System Purpose and Architecture
groups.description: The structured action plan system exists to bridge LLM reasoning and UI Bridge action execution without a second LLM interpretation call. In the standard flow, the agentic-phase LLM calls sdk_ai_execute with natural language, which triggers another LLM call to interpret the instruction. The action plan bypasses this: the agentic-phase LLM directly specifies typed actions with element targets, and the endpoint executes them deterministically. This reduces latency, cost, and ambiguity for multi-step UI interactions. The system was inspired by Skyvern's structured action protocol, adapted for qontinui's cooperative (instrumented) UI Bridge architecture rather than Skyvern's non-cooperative (arbitrary website) approach. The MCP tool documentation in the agentic prompt guides Claude to use sdk_execute_action_plan for 2+ step sequences and sdk_ai_execute for single exploratory actions.

assertions.description: The sdk_execute_action_plan MCP tool is documented in the agentic prompt context, enabling LLMs to discover and use the action plan endpoint during agentic workflow execution

target.label: RUN button (confirms runner is operational and MCP tools are available)

assertions.notes: The MCP tool documentation is embedded in mcp/ai_session.rs as a static string in the prompt context builder. It includes action types, element targeting strategies, caching fields, and a guidance section for choosing between sdk_ai_execute and sdk_execute_action_plan.

assertions.description: UI Bridge steps are allowed in the agentic phase of workflows, enabling action_plan, snapshot, execute, and assert actions alongside AI prompt steps during the verification-agentic loop

target.label: Workflows tab (workflow builder where agentic phase steps are configured)

assertions.notes: Changed in validation.rs: allowed_types_for_phase('agentic') returns ['prompt', 'ui_bridge']. TypeScript UiBridgeStep.phase union includes 'agentic'.

groups.name: Post-Agentic Goal Verification
groups.description: After a successful agentic iteration that included UI Bridge actions (action_plan or execute step types), the unified workflow executor automatically injects a goal-verification-snapshot step into the dynamic steps for the next verification phase. This is an automatic behavior that requires no user configuration. The injected step has name='goal-verification-snapshot', type='ui_bridge', action='snapshot', and carries the agentic outcome summary as ui_bridge_instruction. Previous goal-verification-snapshot steps are removed before injection to prevent accumulation. The behavior only triggers when BOTH conditions are met: the iteration included UI Bridge actions AND the agentic outcome was successful. Source: unified_workflow_executor/loop_handlers.rs handle_post_agentic().

assertions.description: The goal verification snapshot is injected automatically after successful agentic iterations with UI Bridge actions â€” no workflow configuration required. The injected step appears in the next verification phase's step list

target.label: Workflows tab (goal verification activates during workflow execution)

assertions.precondition: A workflow with UI Bridge agentic steps has been run and the agentic phase succeeded at least once. Runner logs should contain 'GOAL-VERIFY: Injecting post-agentic snapshot step'

assertions.description: Goal verification snapshots do not accumulate across iterations. Each successful iteration replaces the previous snapshot step rather than appending, keeping the dynamic steps list clean
assertions.precondition: A workflow with UI Bridge agentic steps has completed at least 2 successful agentic iterations
assertions.notes: Deduplication uses ctx.dynamic_steps.retain(|s| s.name != 'goal-verification-snapshot') before pushing the new step.
